text: Adolescents sleep less than they did a generation ago [1].
Short sleep is linked to poorer next-day recall of new material [2].
Sleep spindles strongly improve memory consolidation in every age group [3].
About 70% of high school students report insufficient sleep.
Later school start times raised average attendance by 9% in a large district trial [4].
Taken together, these results suggest that sleep is a modifiable driver of learning [1, 2].
